overview: Regis Resources is one of the largest gold producers listed on the ASX, mining exclusively in tier-1 Australian jurisdictions. Its production base comprises 100%-owned Duketon (Western Australia, open-pit and underground) and a 30% non-operated interest in the Tropicana Gold Project joint venture with AngloGold Ashanti (70%, operator). Regis also wholly owns the undeveloped McPhillamys Gold Project in New South Wales, one of Australia's largest undeveloped open-pit gold deposits, which is currently held up by a Federal Court legal challenge over a Commonwealth heritage protection declaration.

business_model.summary: Regis is a pure-play, unhedged gold producer that sells 100% of production into the spot market, so revenue and margins move directly with the realised gold price. FY26 production of 379koz generated record revenue of $2,349m at an average realised price of $6,283/oz (AISC $2,945/oz), an EBITDA margin of 57%. The company is debt-free with a $300m undrawn revolving credit facility and ended FY26 with $1.18bn of cash and bullion, giving it unusual balance-sheet flexibility versus mid-tier peers.

revenue_streams.name: Duketon gold sales (100% owned, open pit + underground)

business_model.customer_type: Commodity producer selling refined gold bullion into the spot wholesale market (no hedging, no long-term offtake contracts)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Australian operating assets: Duketon and Tropicana in Western Australia's Eastern Goldfields; McPhillamys development project in New South Wales

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier Australian gold producer (~380koz p.a.) sitting below the ~1Moz+ majors (Northern Star, Evolution) but larger than most junior producers; among the largest ASX-listed gold names by market cap after a record FY26.

moat_factors.description: 100% spot exposure to gold price with zero debt and $1.18bn cash/bullion gives Regis unmatched flexibility to fund growth, sustain dividends, and withstand cost inflation versus hedged or leveraged peers.

100% Australian assets in a tier-1 mining jurisdiction (WA/NSW) eliminate sovereign risk common to many gold miners; six consecutive years of underground reserve replacement exceeding depletion at Duketon.

moat_factors.factor: Large land package / organic growth pipeline
moat_factors.description: ~2,300km² of tenure across the Duketon greenstone belt plus Tropicana's 2,050km² Albany-Fraser belt tenure supports a multi-decade underground exploration pipeline (Beamish South, Ben Hur, Havana).

Regis does not control Tropicana's operating decisions, cost structure, or ESG/community outcomes; AngloGold Ashanti as operator sets the pace of underground development (Havana) and capital allocation at the asset.

weaknesses: McPhillamys — its single largest growth/reserve asset (1.9Moz reinstated reserve) — remains non-producing and subject to an unresolved Federal Court legal challenge, with no guaranteed pathway to development
Two-asset production base (Duketon, Tropicana) is small relative to major peers, limiting diversification and scale economies
AISC guided materially higher for FY27 ($2,990-$3,390/oz vs FY26 actual $2,945/oz), reflecting diesel cost inflation and a weaker Tropicana grade/cost mix
No control over Tropicana's cost base, mine plan or underground development pace as a minority JV partner
Recently walked away from a proposed merger-of-equals with Vault Minerals after Genesis Minerals' competing bid, leaving Regis relatively smaller as peers consolidate into a ~$13bn combined entity

growth_drivers: Underground growth strategy at Duketon: targeting at least four underground mines producing 200-250koz p.a. (Garden Well Main now in commercial production; Rosemont Stage 3 under construction)
BuckWell open pit (Duketon North) ramping up in H2 FY27, expected to deliver ~223koz recovered gold over six years

Sixth consecutive year of underground reserve replacement exceeding depletion at Duketon (Garden Well Underground reserves +257koz/120% replacement in the latest update) and continued replacement at Tropicana (130% underground ore replacement)
New discoveries expanding the pipeline: Beamish South (270koz initial resource, 4km from Garden Well), Ben Hur, Southern Star acquisition
Tropicana Havana underground mine under development, on track for first stope production in H2 FY27, plus ongoing exploration at Swizzler and Havana South

McPhillamys dual-track strategy: pursuing both the original approved project (pending Federal Court judgment) and an alternative Integrated Waste Landform design; refreshed PFS shows 190koz p.a. average production, AISC $1,718/oz, NPV5.5% of $1.13bn and 21.8% IRR at A$4,000/oz gold, targeting FID in H1 CY2028
New Capital Management Policy formalising the balance between shareholder returns and growth reinvestment, following record FY26 dividends of 35cps ($265m, cumulative since 2013 ~$850m)
Optionality for accretive M&A given the debt-free, cash-rich balance sheet, though management has shown capital discipline (walked away from Vault bidding war rather than overpay)

business.description: The Federal Court judicial review of the Section 10 heritage declaration that blocked McPhillamys was heard in December 2025 with judgment reserved as of the FY26 report; an adverse outcome could permanently impair Regis' largest undeveloped asset and $1.9Moz reserve.

Duketon and Tropicana are maturing open-pit/underground complexes; despite strong recent reserve replacement, production sustainability depends on continued exploration success converting resources to reserves.
As a 30% non-operating JV partner, Regis has limited influence over AngloGold Ashanti's cost control, capital allocation and development pace at Tropicana, which contributed ~38% of FY26 production.

business.risk: Failed Vault Minerals merger / consolidation risk
business.description: Regis walked away from a proposed merger-of-equals after a rival bid from Genesis Minerals; sector consolidation is creating larger-scale peers (Genesis-Vault combined ~600-700koz p.a.), potentially leaving Regis relatively sub-scale.

financial.description: FY27 AISC guidance of $2,990-$3,390/oz is materially higher than FY26 actual ($2,945/oz); management notes each 10cpl diesel move affects AISC by ~$25/oz, and diesel spiked in FY26 due to Middle East conflict.
100% spot exposure amplifies upside in a rising gold price environment but leaves earnings and cash flow fully exposed to any gold price correction, with no hedge book to smooth volatility.

FY27 growth capex guided at $250-270m (weighted to H1) for Rosemont Stage 3 and open pit pre-stripping; execution delays or cost overruns could pressure near-term free cash flow, though the balance sheet is well capitalised.

regulatory.description: The Section 10 declaration under the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act 1984 (Cth) that halted McPhillamys illustrates federal heritage law as a binding constraint on major project approvals in Australia, independent of state-level approvals already obtained.
The FY26 report notes a Native Title Determination transition phase at Duketon requiring adjustments to community engagement processes.
First year of mandatory AASB S2 climate disclosure and ongoing work to align with the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management add compliance cost and disclosure risk.

macro.description: Gold hit record highs above US$5,500/oz in January 2026 before falling below US$4,000/oz by late June 2026 — this swing illustrates the sensitivity of an unhedged producer's earnings to macro/rate/USD-driven gold price moves.
Reported in AUD; diesel, labour and consumables cost inflation across the Australian mining sector pressures AISC even when gold prices are strong.

macro.risk: Interest rate and central bank policy sensitivity
macro.description: Gold prices are heavily influenced by real interest rates and central bank buying patterns (record central bank purchases through 2026); a shift toward higher-for-longer rates or reduced central bank demand could compress the gold price and Regis' margins.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold has had an exceptionally strong multi-year run, driven by record central bank buying (Goldman Sachs and other estimates of 700-900 tonnes of official sector purchases in 2026), geopolitical uncertainty, and expectations of policy easing; several banks (Goldman Sachs ~US$5,400/oz, JP Morgan ~US$5,055/oz by Q4 2026) remain constructive, though prices have been volatile within the year (from a January 2026 record above US$5,500/oz to below US$4,000/oz mid-year).
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — gold mining earnings are highly cyclical and directly leveraged to the spot gold price; Regis' unhedged strategy maximizes both upside and downside sensitivity versus hedged peers.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (indirect) — gold prices are inversely correlated with real interest rates; lower rates/weaker USD generally support higher gold prices and Regis' margins, and vice versa.
key_input_costs: Labour and contractor costs (tight WA mining labour market)

recent_developments.event: FY26 annual report released: record NPAT of $715m (up 181% YoY), record EBITDA of $1,345m (57% margin), record operating cash flow of $1,247m, and record dividends of 35cps declared for the year ($265m total), including a 15cps final dividend plus a 5cps special dividend returning the Vault break fee.

Regis lifted FY27 production guidance to 360-400koz but also guided AISC materially higher ($2,990-$3,390/oz vs FY26's $2,610-$2,990/oz guided range) on diesel inflation and a weaker Tropicana cost/grade mix; shares fell ~8% on the announcement despite the production upgrade.

Regis declined to match Genesis Minerals' higher competing cash-and-scrip bid for Vault Minerals, terminating its own Scheme Implementation Deed with Vault and receiving an approximately A$50.7m break fee (returned to shareholders via special dividend); Genesis and Vault proceeded to announce a ~$12.6bn merger-of-equals targeted to complete November 2026.

Released a new Pre-Feasibility Study for McPhillamys demonstrating a viable development pathway (Integrated Waste Landform option) that avoids the disputed Section 10 heritage area, supporting reinstatement of a 1.89Moz Ore Reserve at the project.
Federal Court heard the judicial review of the McPhillamys Section 10 heritage declaration; judgment remains reserved as of the FY26 annual report (August 2026).
Regis and Vault Minerals entered a Scheme Implementation Deed for a proposed merger-of-equals, later superseded by Genesis Minerals' competing offer for Vault.

Garden Well Main and Kintyre moved from development into commercial production during Q3 FY26; sixth consecutive year of underground reserve growth exceeding depletion at Duketon; BuckWell open pit approved and first ore delivered late FY26.

guidance.as_of: FY26 Annual Report / 17 July 2026 ASX Announcement

items.notes: Duketon 240-270koz, Tropicana (30% attributable) 120-130koz; upgraded from prior guidance per 17 July 2026 ASX announcement 'Stronger Production Outlook Lifts FY27 Guidance'.
Up from FY26's guided range of $2,610-$2,990/oz; reflects higher diesel price assumptions (~$25/oz per 10cpl move) and a weaker Tropicana grade/cost mix.
Weighted toward H1 FY27; covers Rosemont Stage 3 underground development and open pit pre-stripping at Duketon and Tropicana.

items.target: At least 4 underground mines producing 200-250koz p.a.
items.notes: Long-term aspirational target assuming no new open pit discovery; strategy expected to sustain delivery into FY28.
Havana underground development targeted for first stope production H2 FY27.

items.target: 190koz average annual production, AISC $1,718/oz, NPV5.5% $1.13bn, IRR 21.8% post-tax at A$4,000/oz gold; pre-production capex $1.08bn
items.notes: Subject to permitting including the IWL and the outcome of the pending Federal Court judicial review; the originally approved project design remains management's preferred option.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman James Mactier and CEO Jim Beyer emphasized record financial performance driven by favourable gold prices and disciplined operational execution, formalisation of a new Capital Management Policy balancing shareholder returns with growth investment, continued underground reserve replacement at both Duketon and Tropicana, and a 'no pressure to transact' stance on M&A given a strong organic growth pipeline following the withdrawal from the Vault Minerals bidding contest. Management flagged FY27 AISC headwinds from diesel prices and Tropicana grade/cost mix even as production guidance was raised.

bull_case: Unhedged, 100% Australian, debt-free producer with $1.18bn cash/bullion gives maximum leverage to a historically strong gold price environment (record central bank buying, bank forecasts of US$5,000+/oz) without the balance-sheet risk many peers carry

Six consecutive years of underground reserve replacement exceeding depletion at Duketon, plus new discoveries (Beamish South, Ben Hur) and Tropicana's Havana underground ramp-up, extend mine life and support the underground growth strategy toward FY28 and beyond

McPhillamys represents a large, optionality-rich call option: a favourable Federal Court ruling or successful IWL permitting pathway could unlock a project with NPV5.5% of $1.13bn and 21.8% IRR at conservative gold price assumptions, with zero cost currently reflected in consensus production
New formal Capital Management Policy and record FY26 dividends (35cps, ~$850m cumulative since 2013) demonstrate a shareholder-return discipline that should continue if gold prices stay elevated
Demonstrated capital discipline — walking away from the Vault Minerals bidding war rather than overpay — reduces the risk of value-destructive M&A that has plagued some gold-sector consolidation
bear_case: McPhillamys remains legally and regulatorily blocked pending an uncertain Federal Court judgment; an adverse ruling would permanently impair Regis' single largest growth asset and 1.9Moz reserve, with the alternative IWL pathway not reaching FID until H1 CY2028 at the earliest

FY27 AISC guidance ($2,990-$3,390/oz) is materially higher than FY26 actual costs ($2,945/oz), driven by diesel inflation and a weaker Tropicana grade/cost mix — margins could compress if the gold price pulls back from cycle highs while costs stay elevated

Fully unhedged spot exposure cuts both ways: gold swung from a record high above US$5,500/oz in January 2026 to below US$4,000/oz by mid-year, illustrating how quickly Regis' earnings and cash flow could reverse in a sustained gold price correction
Tropicana (38% of FY26 production) is a non-operated 30% JV interest, leaving Regis with limited control over costs, development pace and capital allocation at a large share of its production base

Sector consolidation (Genesis-Vault ~$12.6bn merger, ~600-700koz combined production) is creating larger-scale peers, and Regis' decision not to counter-bid for Vault leaves it comparatively sub-scale, which could pressure its relative valuation multiple or ability to compete for future M&A
